entries.knownHazards: The seed of all members of this genus is poisonous[200]. The bark contains a glycoside and a resin that are both poisonous[218]. The seed and seedpod contains a resin and a glycoside called wisterin. They have caused poisoning in children of many countries, producing mild to severe gastro-enteritis[249].
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Sėklos ir ankštys toksiškas — jose yra glikozidas visterinas ir derva, sukeliantys gastroenteritą. Žievė taip pat toksiškas: joje yra glikozidas ir derva.

entries.knownHazards: Although we have found no reports of toxicity for this species, a number of ferns contain carcinogens so some caution is advisable[200]. Many ferns also contain thiaminase, an enzyme that robs the body of its vitamin B complex. In small quantities this enzyme will do no harm to people eating an adequate diet that is rich in vitamin B, though large quantities can cause severe health problems. The enzyme is destroyed by heat or thorough drying, so cooking the plant will remove the thiaminase[172].
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Augale gali būti tiaminazė — fermentas, ardantis vitamino B kompleksą; dideliais kiekiais vartojamas gali sukelti sveikatos sutrikimų. Terminis apdorojimas arba kruopštus džiovinimas fermentą sunaikina.

entries.knownHazards: The roots contain saponins[222]. Whilst saponins are quite toxic to people, they are poorly absorbed by the body and so tend to pass straight through. They are also destroyed by prolonged heat, such as slow baking in an oven. Saponins are found in many common foods such as beans[K]. Saponins are much more toxic to some creatures, such as fish, and hunting tribes have traditionally put large quantities of them in streams, lakes etc in order to stupefy or kill the fish[K].
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Šaknyse yra saponinų, kurie žmonėms blogai absorbuojami ir ilgai kepant sunaikinami. Žuvims saponinai yra labai toksiški.

entries.knownHazards: Many plants in this family are poisonous raw, due to the presence of calcium oxylate crystals. If eaten raw, this toxin gives you a sensation as if hundreds of tiny needles are sticking into the mouth, tongue etc. However, it is easily destroyed by thoroughly cooking or drying the plant. Although no specific mention has been seen for this plant it is wise to assume that it is poisonous in its raw state.

entries.knownHazards: The bulb contains toxic compounds[62]. Horses are said to get the staggers (a cerebrospinal disease) from eating the leaves and bulbs[207].
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Svogūnėlyje yra toksiškų junginių. Arkliams lapų ir svogūnėlių valgymas sukelia smegenų-nugaros smegenų ligą (staggers).
